steps.t: Contractors and suppliers connect with the Cato Client or a clientless browser portal, never a VPN.
The nearest PoP pairs IdP identity with live device posture, re-checked throughout the session.
Compliant users reach only their named apps in the DC and cloud; anything unlisted falls to the block.
Every allow and block lands in Events attributed to the contractor's identity, not an IP address.

steps.t: Priya connects from home or a hotel with the always-on Cato Client, signing in with MFA/SSO via the IdP.
At her desk the Client detects the Cato Socket and switches to office mode; the same rule base applies.
Every path enters the nearest PoP for full single-pass inspection; Microsoft 365 and SaaS egress locally.
Private apps behind the London DC Socket are reached over the backbone, with no VPN concentrator.

steps.t: Managed contractor laptops run the Cato Client with posture checks; unmanaged seats use a browser portal.
Both onramp at the nearest PoP, Johannesburg or Sydney, where ZTNA, RBI and CASB/DLP are enforced.
The private backbone carries repo, VDI and CRM traffic to where the apps are hosted, in the DC and Azure.
DLP blocks source code and customer PII leaving approved apps for personal storage or webmail.

steps.t: Unmanaged devices use a browser on-ramp: the access portal, the Browser Extension or the Enterprise Browser.
Every session terminates at the Cato PoP; the device never receives a route, an address or a network path.
Published private apps and inspected SaaS are reached; DLP blocks downloads and RBI isolates risky web.
Each sign-in, app launch and block is one event attributed to a named user in the CMA.

steps.t: Brandon's always-on Cato Client tunnels to his nearest PoP, Santa Clara, with posture checked continuously.
Microsoft 365 egresses at the PoP; private apps ride the backbone to the London DC Socket.
Client and PoP instrument every segment, so a Fair score is pinned to device, last mile, backbone or app.
Experience Monitoring in the CMA shows per-user, per-app scores before the ticket is raised.

steps.t: SCIM provisions users and groups from Entra ID or Okta into the CMA; synced groups become the policy contract.
Remote users sign in to the Cato Client by SSO with the IdP's MFA; the PoP validates the token.
Behind the Bristol Office Socket the Identity Agent or AD Query names the user behind each IP.
The PoP enforces one identity-scoped policy; unidentified traffic only matches All Unidentified Users.

A second thin dashed line from the IdP to the remote user labelled 'SSO + MFA (OIDC)'. BOTTOM: three data lanes on the LEFT: site() 'Bristol Office' containing 'Priya · Socket X1500' (icon building) with a small 'Identity Agent' tag; 'Warehouse shared PC' sub 'no Client · no AD Query' (icon laptop, cls dash); 'Marcus — remote' sub 'Cato Client · SSO + MFA' (icon laptop).
